settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: buildErrorMessage derives textKey from e.getClass().getSimpleName(), not from a request parameter
LocalizedTextUtil.getMessage/getDefaultMessage resolve the bundle string first and only fall back to defaultMessage; formatWithNullDetection guards against a null literal
The observed flow uses server-side exception/reason text, and existing comments/documentation describe this as standard localized error reporting
candidates.description: JakartaMultiPartRequest.buildErrorMessage (lines 116-120) constructs a LocalizedMessage whose textKey is "struts.messages.upload.error." + e.getClass().getSimpleName() and whose defaultMessage is the exception's getMessage(). This LocalizedMessage is later consumed by localization machinery (see FileUploadInterceptor usage of LocalizedTextUtil.findText(error.getClazz(), error.getTextKey(), ..., error.getDefaultMessage(), error.getArgs())) which, in LocalizedTextUtil.getDefaultMessage (lines 714-737) and findText(ResourceBundle,...) (lines 687-709), treats the resolved message as a MessageFormat pattern and evaluates ${...} segments via TextParseUtil.translateVariables against the OGNL value stack. The concern is that exception messages can embed attacker-influenced request content (e.g. multipart parsing/file-upload exception detail or entity/field-derived text). I could not confirm, from the lines I read, that any part of the textKey or defaultMessage is directly attacker-controlled in a way that reaches OGNL evaluation of untrusted content, so this is reported as a low-confidence candidate for the review focus of untrusted input reaching a message-formatting/expression sink.
missing_evidence: Did not read FileUploadInterceptor.java (lines around 280-330) to confirm exactly how the LocalizedMessage is forwarded to findText and whether any argument is raw request input
Did not read the full JakartaMultiPartRequest/JakartaStreamMultiPartRequest parse logic to determine whether raw FileItem field names/paths flow into the error message
No test or runtime trace demonstrating that attacker-controlled text reaches buildMessageFormat/translateVariables through this path
preconditions: An endpoint uses the multipart parse path where an upload exception message incorporates attacker-supplied data and is surfaced through LocalizedMessage
The message is passed to LocalizedTextUtil.findText with a non-null value stack, so translateVariables evaluates ${...} content
candidates.title: Multipart error message uses exception-derived key/message as i18n lookup/format pattern
